gold.reasoning: 1. Viral or autoimmune myocarditis was considered but made less likely by the absence of infectious symptoms — “He denied any preceding viral illness, sick contacts, or travel.” 2. Inherited or idiopathic cardiomyopathy was included in the differential of new-onset systolic dysfunction — “The differential diagnosis included autoimmune or viral myocarditis, inherited or idiopathic cardiomyopathy, and stress cardiomyopathy amongst other diagnoses.” 3. Stress (takotsubo) cardiomyopathy was considered as a non-ischaemic cause — “The differential diagnosis included autoimmune or viral myocarditis, inherited or idiopathic cardiomyopathy, and stress cardiomyopathy amongst other diagnoses.” 4. Ischaemic cardiomyopathy was initially felt unlikely due to the patient’s youth but suspicion increased with supportive ECG and thrombus findings — “Ischaemic cardiomyopathy was initially felt to be less likely based on the patient’s age, though the presence of an anterolateral infarct pattern on ECG and an LV apical thrombus increased suspicion for a prior ischaemic insult.” 5. Transmural enhancement and aneurysm formation on cardiac MRI pointed to infarction rather than myocarditis or stress cardiomyopathy — “a subsequent cardiac magnetic resonance imaging scan confirmed … full-thickness late-gadolinium enhancement involving all apical LV segments, with apical aneurysm formation in addition to an associated layering thrombus.”

notes: Index visit: the first presentation with several months of exertional breathlessness and leg swelling (s001-s004); the history he gave on transfer to the referral centre (s006, s007) describes events and symptoms before that presentation and is part of the patient's facts.

Vital signs, examination, ECG, repeat echocardiogram and cardiac MRI were obtained on or after transfer (s008-s012) and carry a time; the vital signs and examination were taken after the intravenous diuretics of s005.
Ascites (s009) is kept as an examination finding only: the source does not say the patient noticed abdominal swelling.
The motor vehicle accident and the steering-wheel chest blow are medical-history facts; the chest discomfort afterwards is a resolved symptom with its course as a child.
